manual.title: {{project.name}} Manual
manual.subtitle: What this EPUB studio will be, how the repository keeps its memory, and why it is shaped this way
manual.description: A 3x What / How / Why manual for {{project.name}}. It describes only what exists today: the repository's documentation system and the plan. Planned features live in [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md) until they ship. Current state lives in [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md); durable decisions live in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md).
manual.footer: {{project.name}} {{project.version}} · Built with the 3x Documentation Scheme · Facts cite repository evidence.

sections.title: Foundations
sections.description: How the repository is organised so that any session can pick up the work.

entries.title: Repository memory (the Manifold)
entries.summary: Each kind of project knowledge has one owning document, and a checker keeps them consistent.
entries.what: The project's state, rules, plan, decisions, tests, and security notes live in a small set of Markdown documents, each with one owner and an update trigger. `python3 tools/check_docs.py` fails when they disagree: a missing roadmap or decision ID, a broken link, or a path in the repository map that does not exist.
how: `AGENTS.md` holds the standing rules and the repository map; `CLAUDE.md` only imports it.
`ROADMAP.md` keeps permanent item IDs, `docs/DECISIONS.md` keeps accepted choices with their alternatives, and `docs/HANDOFF.md` is rewritten each time the current state changes.
`docs/README.md` lists which document owns which fact and what change should trigger an update.
entries.why: Recorded in D-007: a fresh agent session starts with no memory, so the repository has to carry it, and a checker is the cheapest way to stop the documents from quietly contradicting each other.

entries.title: This manual (the 3x scheme)
entries.summary: A JSON source builds one standalone HTML manual with a What, a How, and a Why for each topic.
entries.what: The manual you are reading is generated from `docs/plainchant-scribe.manual.json`. Each entry states what something is, how it works, and why it is that way, and cites repository evidence. The generator refuses invalid or placeholder-filled sources.
how: `tools/test_manual.py` tests the generator and checks that this manual builds.
entries.why: Recorded in D-007: the Markdown documents are precise but scattered, and a single explorable synthesis helps a newcomer see the shape before reading the details, at the cost of one more document to keep true.

entries.title: Where the code comes from
entries.summary: Scribe is a spinoff of Plainchant Web; a digest carries the history that still matters.
entries.what: Plainchant Scribe started from a copy of Plainchant Web's source at one named commit, without its git history. A digest records what that project built, which of its decisions still apply to Scribe, and the mistakes that cost it time.
how: The copy was made at roadmap item `P0-02` with `git archive` from the commit hash recorded in D-003, then renamed at `P0-03`.
`docs/archive/plainchant-web-lineage.md` lists the decisions as keep, adapt, or drop, and the gotchas, using a numbering form the documentation checker ignores.
The upstream repository stays the place for full history.
entries.why: Recorded in D-003: a long inherited history would flood a new session's context with features Scribe removes, while a digest keeps the lessons.

entries.title: The manuscript look
entries.summary: One palette of paper and ink in a light and a dark mode, with serif headings and typewriter code.
entries.what: The studio and the home page share a warm paper-and-ink look. Settings offers Match system (the default), Light, and Dark. Headings use EB Garamond, code uses Courier Prime, and dense controls use Inter. The Stage still shows your book on white paper, because the book's own styles decide how it looks.
how: `src/styles.css` defines every colour and shadow as a CSS variable. `:root` is the light palette; the dark palette is written once for the system setting and once for the manual choice, so the page has no flash on load.
`src/app/settings.js` applies the choice as `data-theme` on the root element and sets the browser's theme colour.

`test/theme.test.js` checks that every text, button, and syntax-colour pair reaches 4.5:1 contrast in both modes, that the two dark blocks match, that no colour is hard-coded outside the theme blocks, and that the home page uses the same palette.
entries.why: Recorded in D-008: a book tool is about written pages rather than code, so it gets its own look instead of the inherited dark developer chrome, at the cost of keeping two palettes checked.

sections.title: Direction
sections.description: What the project intends to become, from the plan the maintainer agreed.

entries.title: The plan in brief
entries.summary: An EPUB studio whose book files stay the source of truth, built in eight phases.
entries.what: Plainchant Scribe will let an author make, lay out, check, and export reflowable EPUB 3.3 books. The book's XHTML, CSS, and package files are authoritative and are edited by exact-range splices, never rewritten. Nothing in this entry is built yet.
how: `ROADMAP.md` orders the work: spinoff and renaming, the XML and book format, the Reading Stage, structure tools, layout, import and export with validation, accessibility, and later extras.
Validation is a built-in rule set plus an optional EPUBCheck run in the desktop app (D-005).
Markdown is import only, and Kindle formats are out of scope (D-002, D-006).
entries.why: Recorded in D-002 and D-004: keeping the author's files untouched is the idea that made Plainchant Web trustworthy, and a reflowable EPUB 3.3 target serves most authors with the least moving parts.
